newsitem.title: USA: US Fed OKs interim rule on bank regulatory relief.
newsitem.headline: US Fed OKs interim rule on bank regulatory relief.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Board Wednesday approved an interim rule to exempt well-capitalized bank holding companies from needing approval prior to conducting certain activities.
The interim rule, which the Fed can adjust later after receiving public comment, was effective immediately and implemented the regulatory relief law enacted Sept. 30.

Bank holding companies will no longer have to file applications prior to conducting nonbanking activities allowed under Regulation Y, such as trust company, leasing, tax planning and data processing activities.
The bank holding company will just have to send a notice to the Fed within 10 days after it has started such activity, and no longer requires prior approval, the Fed said.
The interim rule also allowed an expedited application procedure for well-capitalized bank holding companies to acquire businesses that conduct activities permitted under Regulation Y.

Bank holding companies that meet the well-capitalized criteria must provide the Fed with at least 12 business days advance notice of the proposed acquisition or of a proposal to engage in an activity approved only by order, the Fed said.

The Fed defined well-capitalized as a bank holding company with a total risk-based capital ratio of 10 percent or greater and a Tier 1 risk-based capital ratio of 6 percent or greater on a consolidated basis.
The bank holding company would also need to have a Tier 1 leverage ratio of 4 percent or greater.

A minimum Tier 1 leverage ratio of 3 percent would be needed if the firm had a composite 1 rating under the BOPEC rating system or had implemented the risk-based capital measure for market risk, the Fed said.
The Fed seeks public comment on the definition.
"The Board does not believe that the interim rule would have a significant adverse economic impact on a substantial number of small entities," the Fed said.
The Fed is also seeking public comment on how the expedited procedures should be applied to foreign banking organizations.
